sentences.zh: 所以我要从中间开始讲，来自你在喜剧中心频道的《萨拉·西尔弗曼节目》。

sentences.en: And you did this bit, by the way, I don't know if you could do it today.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，你当时演了这段，我不知道现在还能不能播。

sentences.zh: 那是你想要点好消息的一集，所以你决定去做个艾滋病检测，对吧？

sentences.en: And you go, she goes, did you ever have unprotected sex?
sentences.zh: 然后你问，她问，你有没有过无保护性行为？

sentences.en: And you said, is there any other way?
sentences.zh: 而你说，难道还有别的方式吗？

sentences.zh: 然后她说，在80年代，然后你说了。

sentences.zh: 不，对，她说，你有没有在80年代有过无保护性行为？

sentences.en: And I go, oh, my God, yes.
You had unprotected sex in the 80s?
sentences.zh: 你在80年代有过无保护性行为？

sentences.zh: 我说，哦，没有，我还以为你问的是在海地。

sentences.zh: 然后她说，告诉我具体次数。

sentences.en: And so you take a piece of paper and you start writing and you hand it to her.
sentences.zh: 于是你拿出一张纸开始写，然后递给她。

sentences.en: And you go, that's the number.
And she goes, there are two numbers.

sentences.zh: 你说，对，前面和后面各一个。

sentences.en: And she goes, they're the same number.
sentences.zh: 她又说，这两个数字是一样的。

sentences.en: And you said, yeah, I'm kind of OCD like that.
sentences.zh: 你回答，对，我在这方面有点强迫症。

sentences.en: It was like a domino effect of jokes.
sentences.zh: 这就像是笑话的骨牌效应。

sentences.en: It just like started and it was just nonstop.
sentences.zh: 一旦开始就根本停不下来。

sentences.en: And it's such a, you're just, everything about that scene was, again, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 而且它真的是，你整个人，那个场景的方方面面都……再说一次，我不知道。

sentences.en: I think people might be offended today.
sentences.zh: 我觉得现在的人可能会被冒犯到。

sentences.en: There are a lot of problematic things looking back.
sentences.zh: 回顾过去，有很多存在争议的地方。

sentences.en: But, you know, such is comedy.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，喜剧就是这样。

sentences.en: So that's my thing is like, you've always been such a, I don't know, such a fucking stupid word, edgy.
sentences.zh: 所以我的看法是，你一直都是那种——我不知道，这个词真他妈蠢，前卫。
你在做双手合十的手势。

sentences.en: It's always about the messenger of the joke.
sentences.zh: 这总是取决于笑话的传达者是谁。

sentences.en: It's never really about the, so you can say like on the Sarah Silverman program,
sentences.zh: 其实从来都不是关于……所以你可以说，就像在《莎拉·西尔弗曼节目》里一样，

sentences.en: you could do a joke about AIDS like that and people embrace it and laugh because it's you saying it.
sentences.zh: 你可以讲一个关于艾滋病的笑话，大家能接受并付诸一笑，因为这话是从你嘴里说出来的。

sentences.en: So what do you think is the difference between you saying it and somebody else saying it and not getting away with it?
sentences.zh: 那你觉得你讲和别人讲有什么区别，为什么别人讲就过不了关呢？

sentences.en: It seems like you get away with a lot of stuff because you're so fucking funny, but some of it's pretty dark.
sentences.zh: 感觉你总能说很多出格的话，因为你他妈的太搞笑了，但其中有些内容确实挺黑暗的。

sentences.en: I think it's the intention behind it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得关键在于背后的意图。

sentences.en: Like, this is a math term, but it's kind of like the absolute power of the joke.
sentences.zh: 就像，这是个数学术语，但这有点像笑话的绝对值幂。

sentences.en: Like, especially back then, I always said the opposite of what I thought, you know, and that was the joke, kind of.
sentences.zh: 尤其是当年，我总是说反话，你知道的，笑话差不多就是这个意思。

sentences.en: And then hopefully the truth transcends that I don't really feel this way, not to break it down in the least funny possible way.
sentences.zh: 然后希望真相能超越那些我并非真有此意的表象，我可不是在用最无趣的方式去解构它。

sentences.en: But it is also interesting, too, because like that comedy I did, you're right.
sentences.zh: 不过这也挺有意思的，因为就像我以前演的那类喜剧，你说得对。

sentences.en: It was like, oh, it's OK because, you know, I don't mean it.
sentences.zh: 当时的感觉是，哦，这没关系，因为，你知道的，我不是认真的。

sentences.en: But then it also is kind of like we are liberal so we can say anything so we can say, you know, the words that are unsayable or whatever.
sentences.zh: 但同时又有点像，我们是自由派，所以我们可以畅所欲言，所以我们可以说，你知道的，那些平时不能说的话之类的。

sentences.en: Like, you know, I don't mean it so I can say it like there is kind of like a liberal like douchiness about it, I think.
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道的，我不是认真的所以我可以这么说，我觉得这其中有一种自由派式的装腔作势。

sentences.en: And in retrospect, I mean, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 现在回想起来，我是说，我不知道。

sentences.en: I was thinking about that the other day, which is like what's been gone is things have gotten so serious
sentences.zh: 我前几天还在想这个，那就是有些东西已经不复存在了，因为事情变得太严肃了，

sentences.en: because everybody who's not liberal is so serious and so dark and so real about their negativity or hate or racism or whatever it is that it's taken all of that away.
sentences.zh: 因为那些非自由派的人实在是太严肃、太阴暗、太认真地对待他们的负面情绪、仇恨、种族主义或诸如此类的事情，以至于把所有这些乐趣都消解了。

sentences.en: You're like, well, I don't even want to joke about anything.
sentences.zh: 你会觉得，好吧，我甚至什么都不想拿来开玩笑了。

sentences.en: A lot of things that are rough or maybe pushing boundaries because you feel like I don't want it to be taken the wrong way because there are so many people who mean it.
sentences.zh: 很多比较尖锐或者可能在试探边界的事情，因为你会觉得我不想被曲解，因为有太多人是认真的。

sentences.en: You know, it's like so close.
Like people go, oh, it's so funny.
sentences.zh: 就像人们会说，哦，太好笑了。

sentences.en: I saw like a comment in Spanish of something that I wrote and I go, oh, you know, I have a fan that's Spanish.
sentences.zh: 我看到一条用西班牙语写的关于我某个作品的评论，然后我想，哦，你知道的，我有一个西班牙语粉丝。

sentences.en: Then I press translate and it was just, why don't you stick to comedy and, you know, leave politics on it.
sentences.zh: 接着我点了一下翻译，上面写着，你为什么不老老实实说相声，别扯什么政治。

sentences.en: I was like, oh, so wait, I'm sure you've had your share of criticism.
sentences.zh: 当时我就想，哦，等等，我敢说你也承受过不少批评。

sentences.en: Like we all have like positive, negative.
sentences.zh: 就像我们所有人一样，有正面的，也有负面的。

sentences.en: But is there someone in your life that mattered to you who said that you may have taken certain materials too far or something like that?
sentences.zh: 但在你的生活中，有没有哪个对你重要的人说过，你可能把某些段子开得太过了之类的话？

sentences.en: Which of your friends have you offended?
sentences.zh: 你把你的哪些朋友给惹毛了？

sentences.zh: 其实我有些朋友，一开始都是从质疑我、声讨我开始的。

sentences.en: I would guess, and please correct me, but I would guess that one of the things that appeals to you about comedy, about thinking of funny stuff and crafting it into something,
sentences.zh: 我猜想——请随时指正我——但我猜想，吸引你去做喜剧、去思考那些搞笑的东西并把它打造成品的一大核心，

sentences.en: you know, in order to deliver it to an audience,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，为了呈现给观众，

sentences.en: is about identifying that which makes some of us uncomfortable as opposed to some people look, it seems to me, look at other things that makes them excited about comedy.
sentences.zh: 其实就是去找出那些让我们当中某些人感到不舒服的东西；相比之下，在我看，有些人对喜剧产生热情是因为别的东西。

sentences.en: With you, it seems like there, you have an affinity for, as do I, trying to identify the thing that all kind of makes us a little bit uneasy because it's,
sentences.zh: 在你身上，似乎有一种倾向——我也是如此——试图找出那种让我们所有人都感到有点不安的东西，因为它是，

sentences.en: it only exists in our smallest place.
sentences.zh: 它只存在于我们内心最隐秘的角落。

sentences.en: And you want to kind of bring that out and amplify that and share a common sort of reference point.
sentences.zh: 而你想把它挖掘出来、放大，并分享一种共同的参照点。

sentences.en: are you finding that you're frustrated that outside sources seem to be narrowing those borders and those walls and now you have to kind of think twice and three times about that?
sentences.zh: 你是否发现自己感到沮丧，因为外界似乎在缩小这些边界和高墙，以至于你现在不得不三思而后行？

sentences.en: Or do you not listen to that?
sentences.zh: 还是说你根本不理会这些？

sentences.en: Like, if you do something that is risky, you have to be risking something.

sentences.en: Like, you can't get mad that there are consequences.
sentences.zh: 就像，你不能因为有后果而生气。

sentences.en: And I don't mind, I like, like, when young people, you know, like, students or whatever, like, they teach me new language.
sentences.zh: 我不介意，我挺喜欢当年轻人，你知道的，比如学生或者其他什么人，教我新词汇的时候。

sentences.en: I'm into that because I feel like they're always on the right side of history and I want to, like, learn new words and pronouns even though I fuck up all the time.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢这样，因为我觉得他们总是站在历史正确的一边，我想学习新词汇和代词，尽管我总是搞砸。

sentences.en: Fire, by the way, is a new one for something that's good, okay?
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，“Fire”是用来形容某事很棒的新词，好吗？

sentences.en: I had a guy tell me, I had a guy tell me on Twitter, it made me think about, you know, there's an ad that came out for Biden with Sam Elliott doing the voice for it.
sentences.zh: 有个家伙在推特上对我说过一件事，让我想起了一点，你知道的，之前出过一个拜登的广告，是山姆·艾利特（Sam Elliott）配的音。

sentences.en: I don't know if you heard it.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你有没有听过。

sentences.en: I said, the VO master, right?

sentences.en: And I thought, I was like, wait a second.

sentences.zh: 而且这还在我的范围内，我就想：我连对配音发表个评论都不行吗？

sentences.en: Also, like, whoever's saying that, what do they do for a job?
sentences.zh: 还有，不管是哪个说这种话的人，他们自个儿是干什么的？

sentences.en: I hope that they are only a critic.
sentences.zh: 我希望他们纯粹是个评论家。

sentences.en: So, speaking of sticking to what you do, you started, you started doing stand-up when you were young.
sentences.zh: 那么，说到只做好自己的本职工作，你很年轻的时候就开始做单口喜剧了。

sentences.zh: 单口喜剧刚开始的时候，那总是让我惊叹。

sentences.en: I liked it, like, jokes about...

sentences.zh: 你知道，实际上我读的高中，真的……

sentences.en: as long as I shut up the rest of it.

sentences.zh: 不过这也是我愿意承担的盲盒抽奖。

sentences.en: We'd love to get you to repeat that for a PSA if we could real quick.
sentences.zh: 如果可以的话，我们很想让你为公益广告重新录一遍。

sentences.en: You know, when I play basketball, I feel marijuana enhances my game or puts me into a ball,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当我打篮球时，我觉得大麻能提升我的水平或者把我变成一团球，

sentences.en: but either way, it's worth the risk.
sentences.zh: 但不管怎样，这都值得一试。

sentences.en: But you also like to smoke it when you're not playing basketball.
sentences.zh: 不过你平时不打篮球时也喜欢抽。

sentences.en: I like to have a puff at night.
Now, do you follow professional basketball?
sentences.zh: 那么，你关注职业篮球吗？

sentences.en: You know, I like watching it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我挺喜欢看的。

sentences.en: But I mostly like watching, like, a close game in the last half, last quarter.
sentences.zh: 但我大部分时候喜欢看那种最后半场、最后一节比分咬得很紧的比赛。

sentences.en: I'm not—I don't have, like, a team that I'm obsessed with or something.
sentences.zh: 我不是——我没有什么痴迷的球队之类的。

sentences.en: It's tough to watch the first three quarters.

sentences.zh: 我喜欢任何处于劣势的队伍。

sentences.en: I mean, but then again, I also like the Warriors just because I love Steve Kerr and, you know.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，话虽如此，我也喜欢勇士队，纯粹是因为我喜欢史蒂夫·科尔，而且，你知道的。

sentences.en: And I like the Lakers and I like the Celtics, but only just because of various reasons.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢湖人，也喜欢凯尔特人，但纯粹是出于各种不同的原因。

sentences.en: So, Sarah, your resume is so crazy because not only are you an incredible stand-up,
sentences.zh: 所以，莎拉，你的履历太疯狂了，因为你不仅是一位出色的单口喜剧演员，

sentences.en: but you've been part of some just great, memorable shows.
sentences.zh: 而且你还参与过一些非常棒、令人难忘的节目。

sentences.en: You know, SNL, iconic shows, I should say.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，周六夜现场，标志性的节目，我应该这么说。
周六夜现场、《守望先锋先生》（译注：实际为Mr. Show）、《拉里·桑德斯秀》。

sentences.en: I mean, it's incredible that you got to be part of all these things that, for somebody like me,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你能参与所有这些节目真是太不可思议了，对像我这样的人来说，

sentences.en: were shows that really—that really kind of spoke to—
sentences.zh: 这些节目真的——真的可以说是触动了——
天哪，你刚把气氛破坏了。
现在我们永远到不了那种情绪了。
现在我们永远到不了那种情绪了。

sentences.en: But these are shows that, like, you know, Mr. Show and Larry Sanders were—they showed me.
sentences.zh: 但这些节目，你知道的，《Mr. Show》和《拉里·桑德斯秀》它们向我展示了——

sentences.en: I was like, oh, wait, I want to do that kind of shit.
sentences.zh: 当时我就想，哦，等等，我想搞那种破玩意儿。

sentences.en: Yeah, they're like comedy gold shows.
sentences.zh: 对，它们就像是喜剧界的黄金节目。

sentences.en: I mean, I got to be on all of those are iconic shows that I had nothing—you know, I was like a zealig.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我能上所有这些标志性的节目，虽然我没出什么力——你知道的，我就像个福斯特（译注：Zelig，指无处不在的小人物）。

sentences.en: I just got very lucky and ended up in—
sentences.zh: 我只是运气极好，最后进了——

sentences.en: I just, you know, I had nothing to do with creating the—you know, I mean, but yeah, it is.
sentences.zh: 我只是，你知道的，我跟那个的创作没半点关系——你知道的，我是说，不过对，确实是。

sentences.en: I've been in a lot of, like, very cult-y—
sentences.zh: 我经历过很多，那种，非常像邪教的——

sentences.en: Wait, what was your time like at SNL, and do you watch it now?
sentences.zh: 等等，你在周六夜现场的时光怎么样，现在还看吗？

sentences.en: I watch it, and I'm a fan of it.
sentences.zh: 我在看，而且我是它的粉丝。

sentences.en: We can take the pause out in poSt.
sentences.zh: 我们可以在后期把停顿剪掉。

sentences.en: I mean, it's—I had—the year that I was there, I would never want to take back.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我——我待在那儿的那一年，我绝不想收回。

sentences.en: It was, like, hard, and it was long, and it was frustrating, and, you know, but I got along with everybody, you know, and stuff.
sentences.zh: 那段日子，怎么说呢，很辛苦，时间很长，又让人沮丧，而且，你知道的，但我跟所有人都处得很好，你知道的，诸如此类。

sentences.en: It was really a different time, you know.
sentences.zh: 那真是一个不同的时代，你知道的。

sentences.en: I mean, it was—I mean, they didn't have computers.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那会儿——我是说，他们还没有电脑。

sentences.en: Like, we wrote our sketches on legal pads and gave it to a room of typists.
sentences.zh: 就像，我们的短剧都是写在法律专用的记事本上，然后交到打字员的房间。

sentences.en: Well, how did you like living in New York?
sentences.zh: 那你当时觉得在纽约生活怎么样？

sentences.en: I moved there when I was 18.
sentences.zh: 我18岁的时候搬到那儿的。

sentences.en: I love just walking through the streets.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢就那样走在街道上。

sentences.en: Do you wish you still lived there?
sentences.zh: 你希望自己还住在那里吗？

sentences.en: Why do you—because I'd love to live there, but I have to live here for other reasons.
sentences.zh: 你为什么——因为我很想住在那里，但由于其他原因我不得不住在这里。

sentences.en: I'd love to live there, too, but I—I mean, the last time I had an apartment there, it was $450.
sentences.zh: 我也很想住在那里，但我——我是说，我最后一次在那儿租公寓时，房租是450美元。

sentences.en: You know, I lived on a five-floor walk-up where I, you know—we—there was a guy who lived on our floor.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我住在一栋五层没有电梯的公寓里，我，你知道的——我们——我们楼层住着一个家伙。

sentences.en: We had our own bathroom, but it was a building that had a lot of, like, padlocked bathrooms in the hallway that the apartments shared.
sentences.zh: 我们有自己的浴室，但那栋楼的走廊里有很多公寓共用的加锁浴室。

sentences.en: It was a real dark kind of place.
sentences.zh: 那真是一个挺阴暗的地方。

sentences.en: And then this guy who just got out of prison lived in on our floor.
sentences.zh: 然后有个刚出狱的家伙就住在我们那一层。

sentences.en: And my roommate and I were walking downstairs, and he was walking behind us with a friend, and he dropped a box of bullets.
sentences.zh: 我和室友正往下走楼梯，他和一个朋友走在我们后面，然后他掉落了一盒子子弹。

sentences.en: Bullets were just running down our legs, running through our legs down the stairs, and neither of us acknowledged it.
sentences.zh: 子弹就在我们的腿边滚过，穿过我们的双腿滚下楼梯，而我们俩谁都没理睬。

sentences.en: We just acted like it was not happening.
sentences.zh: 我们只是当做没这回事发生。

sentences.en: Sarah, who do you find absolutely hilarious?
sentences.zh: 萨拉，你觉得谁绝对是个搞笑天才？

sentences.en: Like, either growing up or now, like, who are you just like, oh, my God, I can't get enough of blank because they're so funny.
sentences.zh: 不管是成长过程中还是现在，就是那种让你觉得，天哪，我怎么也看不够某某，因为他们太逗了。

sentences.en: If I start off—have you seen Kate Berlant?
sentences.zh: 如果我先说的话——你看过凯特·伯兰特吗？

sentences.en: I love Kyle Dunnigan, this guy Kyle Dunnigan.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢凯尔·邓尼根，就是这个叫凯尔·邓尼根的家伙。

sentences.en: He just—you know, they're people that just make you—
sentences.zh: 他总是——你知道的，这些人就是能让你——
扎克对我来说就是这样。

sentences.en: And then he's just got this huge heart, too, and, you know, he's just like a good, such a solid, lovely person, and he's so funny.
sentences.zh: 而且他这人内心特别善良，你知道吧，他就像是个很好、很踏实、很可爱的人，而且他幽默极了。

sentences.en: What about back in the day, somebody who made you laugh that—well, I guess you can't really say who made you laugh back then, but based on how your sense of humor has changed now,
sentences.zh: 那以前呢，有没有什么人能让你笑得——好吧，我想你大概不能说是谁让你笑的，不过根据你现在幽默感的转变来看，

sentences.en: I mean, there's certainly television shows and movies that I thought were funny back then that I would watch today and go, oh, no, that doesn't hold up.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，确实有些电视剧和电影，我以前觉得挺搞笑的，但现在去看就会觉得，天哪，这根本经不起推敲。

sentences.en: Or my sense of humor has just changed.
sentences.zh: 或者说我的幽默感变了。

sentences.en: I mean, I've gone so many directions.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我的风格变过好多方向。

sentences.en: Like, my friend Mark Cohen, years ago, when I first started, he'd put a nickel on his head and say, Jewish Ash Wednesday, and I cried because I was so sensitive.
sentences.zh: 比如我的朋友马克·科恩，好几年前我刚开始的时候，他会在头顶放一枚硬币，说这是犹太圣灰星期三，当时我都气哭了，因为我太敏感了。

sentences.en: And then I went, like, 180 degrees, you know, but I'm the same inside, you know, but, like, I was so upset by that, you know.
sentences.zh: 然后我来了个180度大转弯，你知道的，但我内心还是那个我，不过当时我真的为此很难过，你知道的。

sentences.en: Yeah, an example of how people change, people's tastes change,
sentences.zh: 对，这就是个例子，说明人是怎么变的，人的品味是怎么变的，

sentences.en: and you kind of have—you find yourself trying not to factor that in when you're thinking of stuff that might be best suited for something that needs to appeal to a wide audience because the people who are financing this don't want it to appeal to a narrow audience.
sentences.zh: 而且你得——你会发现自己在考虑那些需要迎合大众口味的内容时，会刻意不去把这些因素算进去，因为出资方不希望它只迎合一小撮人。

sentences.en: Do you have to fight that?
Well, I mean, that's why I think I prefer to be niche.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，这就是为什么我觉得自己更适合走小众路线。

sentences.en: You know, it's—there's a lot of rules in the mainstream.
sentences.zh: 你知道，主流里有很多规矩。

sentences.en: That's why I'm doing this podcast now.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我现在要做这个播客。

sentences.en: And called the Sarah Silverman PodcaSt.
sentences.zh: 也就是《莎拉·西尔弗曼播客》。

sentences.en: And the one cool thing about it is, like, even if you're on cable or streaming or something, I mean, you can really say anything.
sentences.zh: 它最酷的一点在于，哪怕你是在有线电视、流媒体还是别的什么平台上，我是说，你真的什么都能说。

sentences.en: I think I said fuck way too many times in the first few episodes because I felt so free.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我在前几集里“他妈的”这个词用得太多了，因为我感觉太自由了。

sentences.en: And you have to have the kind of—get those same lessons that you have when you do stand-up where it's like,
sentences.zh: 然后你就得经历那种——吸取你在做单口喜剧时学到的教训，就像是，
现在这纯粹成了一种无意义的废话。

sentences.en: You're using it as a crutch.
But I had to kind of learn it over again because I was suddenly so excited to get to say anything I wanted that I was like,
sentences.zh: 但我得重新适应这一切，因为我当时突然太兴奋了，终于能说任何我想说的话，所以我就一直在那儿，

sentences.en: I listened back and I was just like, ay, ay, ay.
sentences.zh: 我回头一听，就觉得：哎呀呀呀。

sentences.en: What I always thought you did such a great job of doing, you do it when you were, like, on a panel, like on a—your guest on a talk show or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我一直觉得你有一点做得特别棒，比如你在嘉宾座谈的时候，或者上脱口秀节目当嘉宾的时候。

sentences.en: You found ways to—I think a lot of people, you were for a long time considered kind of, like, dirty or you would do—you would dress jokes up.
sentences.zh: 你总能找到方法——我觉得很多人，你在很长一段时间里都被认为有点低俗，或者你会把段子——

sentences.en: You never knew what you—trojan horse, like, you'd come in and you'd dress it up and be kind of super bright about it and then the punchline would be really dark.
sentences.zh: 你永远不知道你要——木马计似的，你出场时把段子包装得漂漂亮亮的，表现得极其聪明伶俐，然后包袱却非常暗黑。

sentences.en: And you found a way to constantly—kind of going back to Sean, I feel I sound like an old man, like you were edgy.
sentences.zh: 你总能找到不断突破的方法——有点像肖恩那样，我感觉自己听起来像个老头子，就好像你很有前卫感。

sentences.en: But you found ways to push the boundary and you didn't necessarily swear, but you did not shy away from making jokes that were hit really hard.
sentences.zh: 但你总能找到打破常规的方法，你未必会说脏话，但你绝不回避那些直击要害的笑话。

sentences.en: Like, everyone would be like, she's a putty-mouther.
sentences.zh: 比如说，大家都会说：她满嘴脏话。

sentences.en: And I guess I am, but, like, I never feel that way because I was raised in a house where you used just the—words weren't taboo, you know?
sentences.zh: 我想我也许是吧，但我觉得从来没有那种感觉，因为我是在这样一个家庭长大的：语言不是什么禁忌，你知道吗？

sentences.en: So it's not like I swear a lot, really.
sentences.zh: 所以其实我并不是经常说脏话。

sentences.en: It's more like I use technical language or explicit maybe, you know?
sentences.zh: 更像是我会用一些专业术语或者比较露骨的词，你知道吗？

sentences.en: You didn't say—you didn't say fuck a lot.
sentences.zh: 你没怎么说——你没怎么说“操”这个词。

sentences.en: You didn't do that at all.
you found a way to bring people to a punchline that was potentially really—they hadn't heard it before and it was kind of dangerous and you were kind of pushing the boundaries.
sentences.zh: 你找到了一种方法，把大家引向一个可能非常……他们以前没听过的包袱，而且有点危险，你有点在挑战底线。

sentences.en: So are there any kind of—Jason asked you if you want to do, like, a drama or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 那么有没有哪种——杰森问过你想不想演，比如，剧情片或者类似的东西。

sentences.en: But are there any, like, comedy people for reals that you would want to work with or comedy directors that you think, like, oh, I can—
sentences.zh: 但是有没有那种，真正的喜剧界人士你想和他们合作的，或者你觉得，哦，我可以——

sentences.en: You know, I haven't done a lot of comedy.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我没演过太多喜剧。

sentences.en: Well, this is the thing is the things I've been in in comedy, like in movies, it's like this has changed a lot.
sentences.zh: 嗯，问题是，我演过的那些喜剧，比如电影里的，这已经发生很大变化了。

sentences.en: But since, you know, it's the angry girlfriend or the angry roommate or the sleazebag executive or—but it's like—so I go—after a while I go,
sentences.zh: 但自从，你知道，总是演生气的女友、生气的室友、卑鄙的高管，或者——但就像是——所以我去——过了一段时间我说，

sentences.en: I just don't even want to be in comedies because the access I have to comedies is—I can't be a comedian in a comedy playing a straight role.
sentences.zh: 我甚至都不想演喜剧了，因为我能接触到的喜剧资源是——我不能在喜剧里演一个正经角色却当不成喜剧演员。

sentences.en: It doesn't—I don't make money from doing movies.
I get the least amount of money.
I can't be on the road, you know.
sentences.zh: 我不能到处跑，你知道的。

sentences.en: So that's why it's, like, dramas or something where I'm in, like, someone else's domain is—it just makes sense.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么，比如剧情片或者其他我身处别人地盘的类型——这反倒合情合理。

sentences.en: I just want to play—if I'm in a comedy, I want to be funny in it.
sentences.zh: 我只想演——如果我要演喜剧，我希望在里面表现得很搞笑。

sentences.en: And otherwise, you know, I just want to do interesting things.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，你知道，我只想做一些有趣的事情。

sentences.en: You know, I like acting, but I like doing everything.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我喜欢表演，但我什么都想尝试。

sentences.en: Sarah, I don't even know where to go.
sentences.zh: 萨拉，我甚至不知道该把话题引向何方了。

sentences.en: I mean, we could talk to you all day.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们可以跟你聊上一整天。

sentences.en: It's so fun having you here.
sentences.zh: 你能来这里真是太有趣了。

sentences.en: You've been talking for so long.
We've taken a lot of your time.
I'm so happy to be just seeing you and talking to you.
sentences.zh: 能见到你并跟你聊天，我太高兴了。

sentences.en: We're going to wrap it up.
But we're going to say you're an absolute delight.
sentences.zh: 但我们要说你绝对是个开心果。

sentences.en: You are a—you're a comic titan.
sentences.zh: 你是一个——喜剧界的泰斗。

sentences.en: I find you to be so fucking consistently hilarious.
sentences.zh: 我发现你一直都他妈的这么搞笑。

sentences.en: You've made me laugh so many millions of times.
sentences.zh: 你让我笑了成百上千万次。

sentences.en: Doesn't it make you feel old?
sentences.zh: 这难道不让你觉得自己老了吗？

sentences.en: I remember when Joan—when you'd go, oh, Joan, you're a legend.
sentences.zh: 我记得琼——以前你会说，哦，琼，你是个传奇。

sentences.en: You know, like it makes you feel done.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这感觉就像你已经被淘汰了似的。

sentences.en: The next thing I do, you know how like your agent will go, ooh, but we got with or and for the credits.
sentences.zh: 接下来我要做的事，你知道经纪人经常会说，哦，但我们在演职员表里争取到了“with”或者“for”。

sentences.en: I want them to fight for that.
sentences.zh: 我希望他们为这个争破头。

sentences.en: My thing I keep going to is I'm asking my—I'm like, I want to fight for—in advance, fight for my position in the—in memoriam segment on like the Emmys and stuff.
sentences.zh: 我一直琢磨的事是，我在要求我的——我就想，我要提前争取——争取在艾美奖之类节目的“缅怀逝者”环节里占据一个好位置。

sentences.en: Oh, I'm already working on my reel.
sentences.zh: 哦，我已经在剪辑我的生平集锦了。

sentences.en: I want to get the final—yeah.
sentences.zh: 我想拿到最后一个压轴的——对。

sentences.en: And I want to bring down the fucking—
Do you know the song, Will?
Do you know the song you want to play?
sentences.zh: 你知道你想放什么歌吗？
五美元一尺长的三明治。

sentences.en: Always, you know, there's that gross word again, but always edgy, dark.
sentences.zh: 总是，你知道，又出现那个恶心的词了，但总是那么先锋、黑暗。

sentences.en: Like, she's the kind of comedy you choose when you really want to—it's like truth comedy.
sentences.zh: 就好像，她的喜剧风格是那种当你真的想要时才会选的——就像是真实派喜剧。

sentences.en: And she's one of the cool kids.
Like, she was just so funny in such a great, real, like, way you're like, shit, man.
sentences.zh: 她就是那种太好笑了，以一种如此棒的、真实的、让你觉得，靠，老兄的方式。

sentences.en: I just don't want to fuck up around her.
sentences.zh: 我只是不想在她面前搞砸。

sentences.en: You know, that's how I always—
sentences.zh: 你知道，我一直都是这么——

sentences.en: I don't want to be unfunny at any moment.
sentences.zh: 我不想在任何时刻显得不好笑。

sentences.en: Yeah, I don't want to be a fucking loser.
sentences.zh: 对，我可不想当个该死的失败者。

sentences.en: Shit, you're so stupid to even think that.
sentences.zh: 靠，你居然会有这种想法，真是蠢透了。

sentences.en: And then I just don't even get out of my car.
sentences.zh: 然后我就索性连车都不下了。

sentences.en: I'd love to go see her do stand-up.
sentences.zh: 我很想去看她演单口喜剧。

sentences.en: I saw her do a stand-up at the Improv in Melrose, and her opening joke was about rape.
sentences.zh: 我曾在梅尔罗斯的Improv喜剧俱乐部看过她表演单口，她的开场笑话是关于强奸的。

sentences.en: Just to sort of drop the flag and say, here it comes.
sentences.zh: 就像是先亮出旗帜，宣告好戏开场了。

sentences.en: So you have to be a fan and be open-minded, but I am, and I'm a huge, huge fan.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须得是粉丝并且思想开放，而我正是，我是她超级、超级大的粉丝。

sentences.en: Well, I think, you know, and she made such a great point.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得，你知道的，她提出了一个极好的观点。

sentences.en: She's made a lot of jokes that, like, has taken people aback over the years or whatever.
sentences.zh: 这些年来她讲过很多笑话，曾经把很多人吓一跳之类的。

sentences.en: It's all about intention, and her intention is good.
sentences.zh: 这一切都在于意图，而她的意图是好的。

sentences.en: She's a good person, and she's going the right direction.
sentences.zh: 她是个好人，而且她正走在正确的方向上。

sentences.en: And she wants—I think that sometimes she has to make jokes like that to kind of shed light on the other side.
sentences.zh: 并且她想——我觉得她有时不得不开这种玩笑来照亮另一面。

sentences.en: And she's got a new podcast, the Sarah Silverman Podcast, and it is great, of course.
sentences.zh: 她有一个新的播客，萨拉·西尔弗曼播客，当然，它非常棒。
而且她是个绝色大美人。

sentences.en: And you know what the third thing is?
sentences.zh: 你知道第三点是什么吗？
